title: One logger instance per module
description: Logger follows the Multiton pattern — one instance per named module, shared across all callers that use the same name. getInstance(name) must return the same Logger every time it is called with the same name, but a different Logger for a different name. Each logger keeps its own message list. Fill in getInstance() and log().
hints: Store instances in a static Map keyed by module name
In getInstance(), create a new Logger only if the key is not already in the map
log() should append the message to this logger's own list
issues: Creating a new Logger object on every call means each caller gets a separate message history
There is no way to share a single logger across multiple parts of the same module
overallGoal: Use the Multiton pattern so that each module name maps to exactly one Logger instance, shared by all callers that request that name.
goals: getInstance() with the same name always returns the identical Logger object
getInstance() with different names returns different Logger objects
Each Logger maintains its own independent message history
